contract: Single-owner leases fenced by the record revision over the ready Store: lease records live in the guarded stream as self-contained non_state_bearing records; claim, hold, renew, release, seize, claim_expired, status, the holder's fenced write and the terminal complete, each as one atomic step on the Adapter (PostgreSQL: one transaction under the head row lock with clock_timestamp() sampled under that lock; Memory: one serialized owner section with a manual clock), with the pure Cure classification, reading, regression gate and decision tables. Sampled-time liveness; revision fencing, not identity.
limits: Liveness is evaluated at the store-clock sample taken under the key's head lock within the transaction that records the change (issue #45 as amended): a renewal sampled before expiry may commit after expiry, and an unlocked status/hold may report the prior lease stale before that commit and the renewed lease active afterwards; no claim of liveness at the physical commit instant and no linearization claim for unlocked readers.

Revision fencing rejects the fence of a superseded lease and cannot authenticate how a current fence was obtained: held values are plain transferable maps, hold/3 has no authentication, owner strings are attribution, not identity; a writer presenting the current revision is not rejected on the basis of holder identity. Expiry alone is not detected by the revision: an expired holder's write commits while no record has moved the head.

claim_expired never grants one key to two concurrently live owners; result sets of overlapping invocations are not necessarily disjoint (a key whose grant ceased to be live may appear twice with different fence revisions). On PostgreSQL a sweep is one transaction (per-key FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, a savepoint FOR UPDATE NOWAIT probe, no head insert); on the Memory double it is one serialized owner section without rollback of earlier per-key commits ({:partial, ...}), a finite approximation of the one-transaction law.

OD-1 Option L schema dependency: Elzoo.Lease.Postgres acts on the integration/sql tables elzoo_log_heads and elzoo_log_records of migration version 1 under the Store's prefix and fails closed ({:error, {:schema, detail}}) on any other table shape (columns with data type, nullability and default; primary keys; the elzoo_head_bounds and elzoo_record_bounds checks as PostgreSQL renders them), checked at new/1, before the first statement of every lease transaction, before the holder's write/4 and before every unlocked read including confirm/2; the rows it writes are ordinary Store records (validate_row, read, replay, confirm, retain unchanged). Outbox items are not supported on the complete/4 path.

The reading uses only the latest lease record below the head; retention that prunes it makes the key ambiguous (pruned_prefix, fail closed) until a seize; retention_bound/2 is an advisory bound and a consumer Need, not a reservation. On PostgreSQL concurrent retention is serialized by the head row lock; on Memory every call of this Piece (lease steps, confirm/2, write/4, complete/4, Elzoo.Lease.Memory.retain/5) goes through the single owner, a second owner per Memory Store is rejected, direct Store calls are outside the supported Contract, retention_observed is after-the-fact detection, not prevention, and a modifying Memory call waits for the owner without a timeout (only read-only calls, including confirm/2, return {:error, :contended}).

Ambiguous keys (future stamp, unreadable record, clock regression, pruned prefix) admit only seize with a closed reason code; the regression gate refuses every other operation, including complete/4, when the sample is earlier than the latest recorded stamp.

Selected laws cover the classification over ordering outcomes and the specification of the comparison; the production comparison (the builtin integer <) is finite-test-grounded against the law-covered structural mirror (all signed pairs in -32..32 and boundary values), not proved; this is not a proof of the production comparison.

Every entry point refuses inside the caller's open Ecto transaction on the Store's Repo ({:error, :caller_transaction}) before any statement; a lock or query timeout before the first write statement is {:error, :contended}, a failure after it is {:indeterminate, info} for confirm/2.

The lease's fold and limits are the Store term's own (passed values must be equal, else {:error, {:invalid, :fold | :limits}}), so every lease row is validated with the settings the Store reads and replays with. Reviewed boundary choices: owner UTF-8 1..200 bytes without NUL; ttl_ms in 1..86_400_000; limit in 1..1_000; at most 1_000 distinct candidates; limits.max_record_bytes >= 1_024 and max_batch_size >= 2; a sweep holds the head locks of evaluated keys until its commit.

No distributed lock service, consensus, cross-store agreement, authorization, TTL policy, sweeper cadence, key discovery or job scheduling; PostgreSQL locking, clock_timestamp() and transaction semantics are upstream contracts; finite scenarios on one local PostgreSQL and the volatile double, not durability or exactly-once claims.

The pinned Cure compiles and audits the production source (no axioms, holes, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or not-proven-total symbols; zero absurd); seven negative controls (FutureStampActive, ExpiryNowActive, ReleaseReadsHolder, RegressionPermits, AmbiguousReleases, StaleRenews, FalseLaw) are rejected at the reflexive line of the named law in the bundled test.

Memory double with the manual clock: selected-law compilation and negative controls; LS1-LS7 (claim, hold, status, renew, release, fence after replacement with the no-takeover control, store-clock-only expiry, seize, concurrent claims, sweep with limit, overlap and partial failure), LS8 (handoff, sampled-after-expiry refusal, admitted late commit with the earlier sample, lost CAS), LS9-LS11 (future stamp, unreadable, unknown holder, lost reply and confirm, superseded, atomic terminal batch and rollback), LS13-LS21 (clock unavailable, validation, pruned prefix, retention through the owner and a detected bypass, self-contained renewal under retention, regression on a free key, the 100->90->95 terminal sequence, comparison agreement, completed receipt, renew batch), confirmation queued through the owner and bounded while it is busy, LS27 duplicate owner; finite scenarios.

Disposable PostgreSQL with clock_timestamp() sampled under the head row lock, database verified before any effect: LS1/LS5, LS4, LS6 (separate connections), LS7 (skipped_locked, free-running sweeps, limit, return-barrier overlap, no head insert), LS8/LS8b/LS8c (renewal across a handoff and across expiry under the lock), LS9/LS10/LS18/LS25, LS11 (lost reply after commit, failure before commit, atomic terminal batch), LS12-LS14, LS15-LS17 (retention serialized by the head lock), LS20/LS26 (unlocked reader stale-then-active), LS22 (helper guard), LS23 (OD-1a schema pin including post-mutation confirmation), LS24 (OD-1b conformance K1-K11 over lease records on both harnesses, replay, confirm, retain), LS28 (absent-head and two-probe races; contender enters a reserved connection before the first insert commits, then grants against the committed free head); finite scenarios.
Local observation printed by the PostgreSQL test: server_version, fsync, synchronous_commit, current_database() and the store-clock offset to the node clock; not a production or all-execution claim.

Relies on the pinned Cure compiler/kernel for the selected equality laws, the inductive Int with native runtime and the builtin integer comparison; the builtin comparison is opaque to the kernel on open terms (established by experiment), hence the structural mirror.
Jason 1.4.5 encodes and decodes the lease payloads (the ready integration/json recipe's direct use); decoding failures are unreadable records.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo.transaction/2, in_transaction?/0, query timeouts and savepoint statements on the checked-out connection are upstream contracts.

PostgreSQL row-level locking (FOR UPDATE, SKIP LOCKED, NOWAIT with SQLSTATE 55P03), clock_timestamp(), READ COMMITTED visibility, ON CONFLICT unique-index waits and transaction atomicity reached through Postgrex 0.22.4 are upstream server contracts, not local proofs.
Elixir validation, exceptions, Task and BEAM execution are upstream contracts, not proved here.
OTP 29.1.2 GenServer, :global name registration, Agent, links/monitors and :crypto are upstream contracts; no exactly-once or disk durability guarantee.

The consumer merges Elzoo.Lease.kinds/0 into its fold, keeps schema_version 1 in fold.versions and never writes those kinds itself; every write to a leased stream goes through write/4, complete/4 or passes the fence revision, with terminal kinds routed through complete/4; retention respects retention_bound/2; on the Memory double all Store calls on leased streams go through the single owner; the Store's Repo is the only Repo of the lease (checked at new/1); one PostgreSQL server clock serves the Store and clock_timestamp().

telemetry.contract: No events emitted; decisions are return values and attributable lease records; the consumer's Ecto Repo emits upstream events.

config.contract: Construction-time Store term, fold, limits, clock binding (:store with the PostgreSQL Store, {:manual, pid} with the Memory double), timeout_ms and the test seams; per-call ttl_ms, limit, candidates and reason within the reviewed bounds; no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: seize/5 (attributable operator takeover with a closed reason code, the single ungated operation) and release/3 as commands, with applied ({:held, ...}/{:free, ...}), refused ({:lease_refused, ...}), failed ({:error, ...}) and unknown ({:indeterminate, ...} with confirm/2 by nonce) results; release is idempotent on free; authority is external (a non-goal); no process, pause or drain.
